derivation: Directly: column 1 has stable z: 1=1, 2=1, 5=0, giving {1,5},{2,5}. Implied: {1,3} in column 1 goes to {1,5}, and {2,3} in column 1 goes to {2,5}. State 4 has column 1 unspecified, so it is compatible with every other state.
Maximal compatibles {1,2,4} and {3,4,5} share state 4. Both have empty class sets, so they are the only primes.
Every size-2 partition fails closure: with {1,2,4} and {3,5}, N({3,5},0) = {3,4} is in no member; with {1,2} and {3,4,5}, N({1,2},0) = {1,4} is in no member. The overlap on 4 is required.

Reduced class 1 = {1,2,4}: N in column 0 is {1,4} and in column 1 is {1,2}, both inside, so both are stable with z=1. Class 2 = {3,4,5}: column 0 is {3,4}, stable with z=1; column 1 is {5}, stable with z=0. Reset 3 is in class 2, which is stable in column 0.
not_closed: {1,2,4},{3,5} fails because N({3,5},0)={3,4} is in no member; {1,2},{3,4,5} fails because N({1,2},0)={1,4} is in no member.
